fields.title: Market Outlook 2026: Staying the Course
fields.excerpt: Our research desk's view on markets heading into the rest of 2026, and what it means for index investors.

content.value: Markets have been volatile through the first half of 2026, but the case for staying invested in a diversified, low-cost index fund remains as strong as ever.

Trying to time the market is difficult even for professional investors. A simple, consistent contribution plan into a broad index fund has historically outperformed most attempts to trade around volatility.

fields.excerpt: Yield & Co launches a new tax-free savings account option tracking a broad equity benchmark.

content.value: We're pleased to announce a new fund option available inside our tax-free savings account, tracking a broad, diversified equity benchmark.
Existing TFSA holders can switch into the new option at no cost, and new investors can select it when opening an account.

fields.title: Index Investing 101: The Basics
fields.excerpt: A plain-language introduction to index investing: what an index fund is and why costs matter.

content.value: An index fund simply aims to track the performance of a market benchmark, rather than trying to beat it by picking individual winners and losers.
Because index funds don't need large research teams making active bets, they can be run at a much lower cost — and lower costs mean more of the return stays with you.

fields.title: Yield & Co Cuts Fees Across Core Funds
fields.excerpt: Yield & Co reduces total expense ratios across its core equity and bond index funds from March 2026.

content.value: From this quarter, we're reducing the total expense ratio on our core equity and bond index funds, passing the savings directly on to investors.
No action is required from existing investors — the new, lower fees apply automatically to your existing holdings.

fields.title: Flexible Contributions
fields.body: Contribute what you can, when you can, up to the annual and lifetime limits set by SARS.

fields.question: How much money do I need to get started?

content.value: There is no minimum lump sum required. Many investors start with a small monthly contribution and increase it over time.

fields.question: How do I open an account?

content.value: You can open an account online in a few minutes. You'll need your South African ID, proof of address and a bank account in your name.
It depends on your goals and time horizon. A broad market index fund is a reasonable starting point for most long-term investors.

fields.question: Can I change or cancel my contributions?

content.value: Yes. You can increase, decrease, pause or stop your recurring contributions at any time from your account.
A tax-free savings account (TFSA) lets you invest without paying tax on the interest, dividends or capital gains you earn inside it.

fields.question: How much can I contribute each year?

content.value: SARS sets an annual contribution limit as well as a lifetime limit. Contributions above these limits are taxed at a penalty rate.

fields.question: Can I withdraw money from my TFSA?

content.value: Yes, you can withdraw at any time, but withdrawn contribution room is not restored — it still counts toward your lifetime limit.

fields.question: Can I have more than one TFSA?

content.value: Yes, but your combined contributions across all your TFSAs, at any provider, may not exceed the annual and lifetime limits.

fields.question: What happens if I exceed the limit?

content.value: SARS charges a penalty tax of 40% on any amount you contribute above the annual or lifetime limit, so it pays to track your contributions.
